In Poplar, Abbotsford, the 55+ homes you can buy are Central Heights Manor, Crown Point and Maplewood Estates (strata and manufactured-home park). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is retirement residence or care. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Poplar
Central Heights Manor — 33535 King Rd
Freehold strata plan NWS3075, 3 levels, built 1990; listings describe a 55+ community, and building-source data records "No Pets or Rentals" in its bylaws summary.
Crown Point — 1450 McCallum Rd
Gated townhouse complex, freehold strata plan NWS2984, built 1989, zoning RM30.
55+ manufactured-home parks in Poplar
Maplewood Estates (also listed as Maplewood Mobile Home Park) — 2035 Martens St
Listings for homes in this park use both names for the same address and describe an "Adult Community — 55+": a small pet is allowed and the buyer must be approved by the park owner before purchase.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in Poplar (not for sale)

items.t: Maplewood House — 1919 Jackson St: Long-term care home run by the Maplewood Care Society: 78 beds (all publicly funded; 76 single-occupancy rooms in the Seniors Advocate data), opened 1989, accredited, funded primarily through Fraser Health with all admissions coordinated through Fraser Health — there is nothing to buy and no private application route to the home itself.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Poplar

items.t: The sub-area sits south of Highway 1 around Huntingdon Road, King Road and Gladwin Road, west of the Marshall Road / McCallum Road area and east toward Clearbrook Road; exact board boundary lines are not published in text form — they are shown in the City's interactive WebMap.
The two 55+ strata complexes in are the exception, not the pattern.

The hospital is immediately north across Highway 1: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Road (emergency, surgery, maternity, 24 hours). The Abbotsford Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 100-2692 Clearbrook Road.

BC Transit Central Fraser Valley routes through or beside Poplar: route 3 (Clearbrook / Huntingdon, via the Gladwin and King Road area), route 5 (Clearbrook / Bourquin via Hospital, on Marshall Road at the east edge), route 6 (Gladwin Road corridor) and route 12 (UFV / Bourquin via Jackson Street and McCallum Park and Ride). There is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express in Abbotsford.

Schools physically in the sub-area: South Poplar Traditional Elementary (32746 Huntingdon Road), Jackson Elementary (33165 King Road) and Abbotsford Traditional School, middle/secondary (2272 Windsor Street); SD34 locator runs for both elementary addresses return Jackson Elementary → Abbotsford Middle → Abbotsford Senior Secondary for the regular stream (SD34 School Locator, run 2026-11-01).

The south edge is rural: lots toward Huntingdon Road are in or beside the Agricultural Land Reserve, and Poplar drains toward the Sumas Prairie system, so floodplain status is a lot-by-lot WebMap check (Zoning Bylaw Schedule E), not an area-wide answer.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Poplar

items.t: In a BC strata, "55+" is the only age restriction that still exists: The Strata Property Act (ss. 123.1/123.2, via Bill 44) has allowed only 55-and-over residency bylaws since Nov 24, 2022; older buildings' 19+, 40+ or 45+ bylaws are invalid, which is why any pre-2022 document for Central Heights Manor or Crown Point that shows a different age should be re-read against the current registered bylaws.
Owning is not the same as living in the unit: The Province's guidance: an under-55 person can own a strata lot in a 55+ corporation but may not be able to reside in it — the bylaw controls occupancy.

Who is exempt (Strata Property Regulation 7.01): residents who lived in the unit when the bylaw passed (legacy), live-in caregivers, and — after the May 1, 2023 expansion — the qualifying resident's younger spouse or partner, children under 19 in that resident's care, and adult children the resident cared for before age 19.

Maplewood Estates runs on the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, not the Strata Property Act: BC's page states the Act covers most manufactured home tenancies: the buyer owns the home, rents the site, and the park owner must approve a purchaser (the park's listings say exactly that). Site rent may be increased only once every 12 months, with at least three full months' notice, capped at the annual provincial limit (2.3% for increases effective in 2026; 2.2% announced for 2027) plus a proportional amount for changes in local government levies and regulated utility fees.

If the plan is to age in a Poplar house instead: Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014, s.140.3.8 permits one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings (City reports state the criteria include a minimum 400 m² lot and 12.0 m frontage) — the suite is the usual route to a caregiver or family member on the same lot.

Rural south-edge lots: where the A1 (Agricultural One) zone applies, the minimum subdivision lot area is 8.0 ha, and ALR land adds Agricultural Land Commission Act and ALR Use Regulation controls on subdivision and added dwellings — relevant if a buyer hopes to split a Huntingdon Road parcel for family.

Tax mechanics: Abbotsford tax is the BC Assessment value multiplied by a rate per $1,000 (Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026); taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty September 16, 2026.

Good to know about Poplar

items.t: The City doesn't call this area "Poplar." Its official profile name is "South Poplar" (profile area 5); "Poplar" is the real estate board's label. A buyer reading City documents, census profiles or demographic reports should search "South Poplar" or find nothing.

Three "Maplewoods," three tenures, two sub-areas. Maplewood Manor (Tims Ave, Abbotsford West) is a buyable 55+ strata; Maplewood House (Jackson St, here) is a Fraser Health-funded care home with 78 beds; Maplewood Estates (Martens St, here) is a 55+ manufactured-home park where you rent the pad. Search results blend all three — check the street before booking a viewing.

Poplar is about to hold the city's biggest care construction. The new long-term care community beside Maplewood House at 1919 Jackson St will hold the 109 Cottage/Worthington beds plus 91 new ones — 200 beds on one Poplar site — with a 49-space child care facility built alongside; Fraser Health expected completion in 2027. For a 55+ buyer, that is the sub-area's care backstop arriving on a fixed schedule.

The "Central Abbotsford" mislabel on Central Heights Manor is structural, not a typo in one listing. The same feed error recurs across portals; the building directory's Poplar list and the King Road address are the reliable anchors, and the strata plan number (NWS3075) never changes.

The Traditional school pathway runs through this sub-area. South Poplar Traditional Elementary is one of only two feeder schools for Abbotsford Traditional School (Grades 6–12), and feeder students are automatically registered there — a draw for grandparents buying near family, and a detail the regular catchment (Jackson Elementary) does not capture.

Poplar's name is literal. The community was named for the poplar trees planted on top of the hill, and the Old South Poplar School is on the Abbotsford Community Heritage Register — the rural character at the south edge, where A1 zoning sets an 8.0 ha subdivision minimum, is policy, not an accident of development timing.

faq.a: Two strata complexes (Central Heights Manor, 33535 King Rd; Crown Point, 1450 McCallum Rd) and one manufactured-home park (Maplewood Estates, 2035 Martens St). That is the whole verified buyable 55+ stock in the sub-area — Abbotsford West has fifteen verified 55+ strata complexes, so most 55+ buyers who want selection end up looking there.
faq.q: How much 55+ choice is there in Poplar, honestly?

faq.a: Yes, under the provincial exemption for a younger spouse or partner of a resident who meets the age requirement — Strata Property Regulation 7.01 covers that case, along with legacy residents and live-in caregivers. Crown Point's own MLS data records its pet bylaw (one cat or dog, with restrictions); confirm the age-bylaw wording in the registered bylaws.
faq.q: My partner is 50. Can we live at Crown Point?

faq.a: The strata plan (NWS3075) is the stable identifier.
faq.q: I read Central Heights Manor is "in Central Abbotsford." Which is it?

faq.a: You buy the home, not land: the site is rented under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, the park owner must approve you as a buyer (the listings state this), one small pet is allowed, and pad rent can rise only once a year on three full months' notice within the provincial cap (2.3% for 2026) plus the proportional levy/utility share. It is a tenancy relationship, with none of the Strata Property Act's Form B, depreciation report or strata-meeting machinery.
faq.q: What's different about buying in Maplewood Estates?

faq.a: Yes — ownership is not restricted, only residing is. An under-55 buyer can own at Central Heights Manor or Crown Point but could not live there until meeting the bylaw or an exemption.
faq.q: Can I buy under 55 and hold the unit until I qualify?

faq.a: The sub-area's seniors housing beyond ownership is care housing (Maplewood House long-term care), which is Fraser Health-funded and admission-based, not a rental application. The nearest verified subsidized seniors residences are the Cottage and Worthington Pavilions in Central Abbotsford — themselves scheduled to be replaced by the new care community rising at 1919 Jackson St in this sub-area.
faq.q: Is there any 55+ rental building in Poplar if I don't want to buy?

faq.a: Poplar drains toward the Sumas Prairie system, which the City describes as low-lying and subject to Nooksack River overflow flooding; that description belongs to Sumas Prairie itself, and a specific lot's floodplain status is only settled by the Zoning Bylaw Schedule E map in the City WebMap — check it before subject removal on any low-lying or rural lot.
faq.q: Does the floodplain touch Poplar homes?

faq.a: BC Transit route 5 (Clearbrook / Bourquin via Hospital) runs Marshall Road at the sub-area's east edge, and route 12 serves Jackson Street toward Bourquin Exchange; the hospital at 32900 Marshall Road is immediately north of Poplar across Highway 1.
